sentences.text: The appeal is filed after the delay of 3034 days.
The appellant filed IA.No.1/2023 under Section 5 of the Limitation Act to condone the delay.
It is annexed with an affidavit filed by AGM (HR & Admn.) of appellant- Company.

The reasons assigned in the affidavit are that,
the impugned judgment required certain corrections,
therefore, they filed an application under Section 152 of C.P.C., before the trial Court; the said application was disposed of on 04.02.2016; the appellate obtained certified copy of the judgment and award in the month of February 2016 and it was handed over to the department by its counsel on 03.03.2016; same was sent to Head Office, New Delhi, for taking suitable decision.

Some of the officers in-charge of the case took voluntary retirement,
therefore, the successor in the office could not get the file in time.
In view of these reasons, there is delay in filing the appeal.
Hence, prayed to condone the delay.
3. The respondents filed objections to the said application.
They denied the contents of the affidavit.
They contended that there is an inordinate delay, which is not explained by the appellant.
There are no justifiable reasons to condone the delay of ten and half years in filing the appeal.
Unless the delay is explained properly, it cannot be condoned.

With these reasons, they prayed to The Divisional Engineer vs Sri. Srinivasa Kantharaje Urs on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89364308/
3 dismiss the application.

sentences.text: 4. We have heard the arguments of learned counsel for both parties.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that delay is properly explained in the affidavit filed in support of IA.No.1/2023.
The Hon'ble Apex Court time and again held that condonation of delay application should be considered liberally and shall be condoned.

In support of his submission, he relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Ltd., -vs- Kumaon Entertainment and Hospitalities Pvt. Ltd.,1 and in Delhi 1

from the date of taking of possession of the property and not from the date of Preliminary Notification.

sentences.text: It is settled principle of law that delay has to be properly explained.
However, if we go through the affidavit filed in support of the application, there is no proper explanation nor satisfactory reasons are stated to condone the delay.

It is true that delay application should be considered liberally,
but that does not mean that party cannot take it for granted without even assigning justifiable reasons to condone the same.

He also relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of 2  AIR 2023 SC 3421  -6-  MFA No.6968 of 2023 The Chief Engineer, K.N.N.L., IPC Zone and others -vs- Vishwanath and others3 and in the case of P.K.Ramachandran -vs- State of Kerala and others4 and prayed for dismissal of the application.
 7. Section 5 of the Limitation Act reads as under :
 " 5. Extension of prescribed period in  certain cases :- Any appeal or any application,
 other than an application under any of the provisions  of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5  of 1908), may be admitted after the prescribed  period, if the appellant or the applicant satisfies the  court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring  the appeal or making the application within such  period.

8. Undisputedly, there is delay of 3034 days in filing the appeal.

Learned counsel for the respondents submits that the said calculation is incorrect, however, on 3  MANU/KA/2200/2024 4  MANU/SC/1296/1997  -7-  MFA No.6968 of 2023 reconsideration of the same, period of delay calculated by the office is proper and appeal is filed after delay of 3,034 days.
 9.
The contents of the affidavit which are mentioned in the above paras shows that the affidavit was filed very casually.

The appellant makes grievance about the trial Court taking time for about one and half years in considering the application filed under Section 152 of C.P.C., for correction of the impugned judgment and decree.
But thereafter, appellant took nearly seven to eight years time to file the appeal.
There is no satisfactory explanation as to why they did not/could not file the appeal immediately after obtaining the certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree.

10. Appellant is a Corporation established by the Government of India, having team of legal officers, who The Divisional Engineer vs Sri. Srinivasa Kantharaje Urs on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89364308/
6 could take care of the litigations.

Particulars are not furnished regarding retirement of concerned officers,

Therefore, the reasons assigned that some of the officers who were in-charge of the case took voluntary retirement and in-charge officers could not trace the files cannot be a justifiable ground to condone the delay of about nearly ten years in filing the appeal.
11. The reasons assigned in the affidavit filed in support of application indicates the casual approach of the appellant towards litigation.
There are no justifiable reasons or satisfactory reasons to condone the delay of 3,034 days in filing the appeal.

12. In the Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Ltd., case (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court held that,
 " if there is delay in filing the appeal due to  repeated filing of review application by the appellant  both before the Single Judge and also before the  Division Bench and if such delay is satisfactorily  explained, the delay ought to be condoned."
 (Emphasis supplied)

sentences.text: the said judgment is not applicable to the facts of the present case.

13. In the present case, the land was acquired by issuing Notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, on 09.05.1984, final notification under Section 6(1) of Land Acquisition Act was published on 06.06.1987 and award was passed on 09.09.1998.
The appellant for whose benefit the land was acquired slept over its right for about ten years after passing of the award by the Reference Court.
The land losers are not able to get compensation even after lapse of 40 years from the date of acquisition of land.
All these facts indicate that unnecessarily the appellant protracted the litigation.
Considering all these facts, it is not a fit case to consider the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act liberally to condone the delay of 3034 days in filing the appeal.

14 . Therefore, we proceed to pass the following order:
 - 10 -  MFA No.6968 of 2023  ORDER
The application - IA.No.1/2023 filed by the appellant under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, is hereby rejected.
